question: Should OpenClaw allow scheme-level wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*` for Gateway Control UI origins, or keep extension access limited to exact origins and the dedicated `/browser/extension` route?
rationale: This changes the browser-origin trust boundary and config grammar for Control UI/WebChat, which repository policy treats as security/product-owned rather than a safe autonomous bug fix.

options.title: Constrained pattern contract
options.body: Keep this open only for a schema-validated, documented, audited pattern design with negative security tests instead of ad hoc prefix matching in `allowedOrigins`.

options.title: Exact origins plus extension route
options.body: Narrow or close this direction if maintainers want Chrome extension access handled by exact custom-scheme matching and `/browser/extension` pairing.

options.title: Allow scheme wildcard in place
options.body: Accept `chrome-extension://*` directly in `allowedOrigins`, with the explicit tradeoff that all Chrome extension origins can reach the authenticated WebSocket gate.

recommendation.title: Constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open only for a schema-validated, documented, audited pattern design with negative security tests instead of ad hoc prefix matching in `allowedOrigins`.
